META.subject: General Science
META.titleDoc: GENERAL SCIENCE GRADE 10: RATES OF REACTIONS
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 2.5 • 13 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Plan controlled comparisons,record actual actions,analyse rates/graphs and distinguish mechanisms from unsupported generalisations.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative process engineering,food production and laboratory quality roles.
UNIT.focus: Rates of reactions; Factors affecting the rates of reactions
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional process poster claims every increase in heat,pressure,light or concentration always improves all reactions and that supplied data prove an experiment was performed.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Time-volume records,conditional supervised open-cup endpoint comparison,enzyme/gas/catalyst examples and constrained process choices.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: How do various factors affect the rate of reactions?
UNIT.content: Rates of reactions; Factors affecting the rates of reactions
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses with peers the factors that affect the rate of chemical reactions.
Digital literacy: as the learner uses digital devices and print media to research on the importance of optimum conditions in biological, chemical and physical processes.
UNIT.values:
Responsibility: as the learner carefully uses digital devices to search for information on the importance of optimum conditions in industrial processes.
Respect: as the learner respects others’ opinion while discussing with peers in a group the importance of efficient industrial processes.
UNIT.pcis: Safety and security: as the learner observes safety measures when carrying out activities to investigate rates of reactions.
UNIT.subject: General Science
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
describe rate of chemical reactions,
perform experiments involving the rate of chemical reactions,
explain factors that influence the rate of reactions in biological, chemical and physical processes,
appreciate the importance of manipulating factors affecting the rate of chemical and biological processes in day-to-day life.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Independent40minutes:4readRR13,14Section1,10Section2,6Section3,6Section4/check/submit. Use only final reference/prompts. No answer hints or teacher keys. Practical outcome b requires separately observed approved experiment,not this written final.

sections.title: 1. Quantitative rate evidence
sections.prompt: From RR13 draw a labelled time-volume graph,calculate the four10s interval average rates and overall0–30s average. Find P/Q mean endpoint times,ranges and1/mean time indices to3significant figures with units. Compare processes and state what the plateau and indices cannot prove.
sections.exemplar: Graph points:(0,0),(10,12),(20,20),(30,24),(40,24). Interval rates1.2,0.8,0.4,0cm³/s;overall0–30s0.8cm³/s. Pmean50s,Q30s;ranges4s;indices0.0200s−1 and0.0333s−1. Q reaches the defined endpoint faster. Plateau does not establish cause/exhausted reactant;reciprocal times are not gas-volume rates or intrinsic constants.

sections.title: 2. Factors with conditions and limits
sections.prompt: Explain how each of temperature,pressure,catalyst,light,concentration andsurfacearea can affect an appropriate process,with a relevant limitation for each. Use RR13 enzyme data to identify the highest tested condition and explain why an exact biological optimum is not established. Distinguish one physical-rate process from chemical product formation.
sections.exemplar: Temperature can increase kinetic energy and the fraction of encounters overcoming activation barriers,but enzymes may lose activity at high temperature. Compressing a relevant gas can increase reactant concentration and encounters;adding inert gas at fixed volume/temperature does not. A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation barrier,not a changed equilibrium. Suitable absorbed light can excite species or initiate photochemical changes,not every reaction. Greater reactant concentration can increase encounter frequency,depending on the reaction/range. Greater exposed surface gives more interface sites for a heterogeneous reaction at fixed mass,not a universal exact rate multiplier. Enzyme35°C has highest supplied8units;intermediate temperatures and uncertainty are needed for an exact optimum. Dissolution or evaporation can be physical without new substances. These mechanisms are explanatory models,not directly proven by the fictional records.

sections.title: 3. Fair planned experiment and performance scope
sections.prompt: Propose one teacher-approved rate comparison:state changed variable,measured operational quantity,at least two controls,repeats and two safety conditions. Explain how actual observed actions would be recorded and why this final answer does not satisfy performed-experiment evidence. No pressure vessel,unsafe chemicals or heating procedure.
sections.exemplar: A conditional approved open-cup identical-tablet endpoint comparison can vary teacher-prepared safe water temperature,measure defined visible-bubble endpoint times,hold water amount/tabletbatch/cup/endpoint/mixing fixed and repeat3times. Product/risk/supervision approval and open containers/no ingestion/no heating are required. Record actual observer/date/role/temperatures/times/deviations or not performed. A written plan alone does not meet outcome b. Equivalent safe controlled plans need explicit approved provision.

sections.title: 4. Appropriate conditions in daily use
sections.prompt: Use RR13 industrial facts and budget to make a qualified choice. Explain why fastest is not automatically best,identify two missing decision facts and give one daily-use example with a condition/safety limit. State whether any actual digital research or process manipulation occurred in this final.
sections.exemplar: A fits5tokens/hour;B costs9anddoesnot. Quality,safety,emissions orrealcosts remain unknown,so no best-overall verdict. Cooling may slow spoilage but does not sterilise food or guarantee safety. Written records do not show actual digital research or process manipulation.
